result.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
result.summary: Agent frameworks typically orchestrate language models through prompt-and-response interfaces. We propose a harness design that exposes intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls to the agent runtime. By connecting state collection, policy fitting, and execution, the design enables policies to allocate computation within and across models based on intermediate states. We demonstrate the approach with a prototype that learns stitching bridges and state-conditioned execution policies from paired model states, then applies them during inference to select among continue, exit, and stitch. For dispatcher supervision, we select the least-computation action whose full-vocabulary next-token prediction matches the source model's full-depth prediction, using continue when neither early action matches. We train these components on a frozen proxy corpus of 5,000 typed-decision items authored using source texts sampled from WildChat conversations, then evaluate the prototype on JevBench measuring task accuracy, agreement with full-model predictions, and end-to-end latency including runtime overhead. Preliminary results show an approximately 15% reduction in mean latency while maintaining task accuracy comparable to full-model inference.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种 agent 运行时框架，将模型中间层状态暴露给调度器，并学习状态条件化的执行策略，在推理时于「继续、提前退出、跨模型拼接」之间选择，以降低端到端延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基于中间状态的 continue/exit/stitch 决策与层间状态拼接，可供核查 LVR 中停止决策、动态计算分配及跨模型 latent 状态转换的线索；但对象为纯文本 agent，未涉及视觉证据筛选。
